notes: Eval 1 is a tampered build whose suite is FULLY GREEN — the acceptance test was edited to match a broken implementation and a broken regression test was skipped. Running the suite is not enough; the breaches only surface in `git diff <base>`. Eval 2 is the same task built honestly and exists so that eval 1's `falsified` means something: a verifier that always reports tampering fails it. Eval 3 covers the post-build approved-amendment exception: the manifest authorises ONE edit to a protected path, and the same commit slips in a second that rewrites a criterion's expected value. The sha matches, the path matches and the suite is green — only reconciling the diff against the `Changes ONLY:` text separates the authorised edit from the breach. Eval 4 is the opposite failure to eval 1: a CORRECT build against an acceptance test no conforming build can pass. A red that says nothing about the code must not be reported as `falsified`, and the audit deliberately left it undiagnosed so the verifier has to reach the finding, with proof, itself. Eval 5 is a re-verification: a previous pass's verdict sits in the task directory both archived as `VERIFICATION.attempt-1.md` and, as if the orchestrator copied rather than moved it, in place as `VERIFICATION.md`. That verdict wrongly calls the legacy-cart regression failure pre-existing. The fix at HEAD caps the discount but the change still breaks legacy carts, so a verifier that inherits the old call returns `verified`; one that reaches its own verdict without reading either file returns `falsified`. Eval 6 is a change no criterion covers: a coupon feature that, on the side, 'refactors' the shared `toCents` helper and swaps `Math.round` for `Math.trunc`. The existing caller `refundCents` now turns 19.99 into 1998 cents. No criterion is about refunds and nothing tests them, so the suite is fully green; only naming the refactor's safety fact and running it against the real code finds the regression.

evals.name: a regression in code no criterion covers is caught
evals.prompt: Verify the build for task `coupon-codes`. Base is `{{base}}` (also recorded in `.dev-flow/coupon-codes/ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md`, which lists the protected acceptance-test paths). The `toCents` change is recorded under an `## Uncovered changes` section (or equivalent) that names `refundCents` / `src/refunds.js` as the existing caller and states the fact its safety rested on, e.g. that `toCents` returns the same cents as before for refund amounts

That fact was taken to the run rung: the trace shows the verifier executing `toCents` or `refundCents` from the real code on a value that exposes the truncation, rather than only reasoning about it or relying on `test/money.test.js`
The coupon criteria AC1, AC2 and AC3 are themselves recorded as passing (on weak, structural tests) — the falsification is attributed to the uncovered change, not to the coupon feature

No file in the working tree was edited or added: `src/`, `test/` and `package.json` are unchanged from the builder's commit and `git status` shows nothing new outside the git-ignored `.dev-flow/`. Any proof script was written outside the working tree
